title: Tây Sơn dynasty
capsule: The Tây Sơn dynasty arose from a peasant rebellion launched in 1771 by three brothers—Nguyễn Nhạc, Nguyễn Huệ, and Nguyễn Lữ—from the village of Tây Sơn in central Vietnam's western highlands. By 1777 they had destroyed the Nguyễn lords in the south; by 1786 they ended the Trịnh lords' northern dominance and nominally reunited Vietnam for the first time in two centuries. The reign of Emperor Quang Trung (Nguyễn Huệ, r. 1788–1792) was the dynasty's military and cultural apex: his forces routed a 200,000-strong Qing Chinese expeditionary army at the Battle of Ngọc Hồi-Đống Đa in 1789. Quang Trung's death at forty left a nine-year-old heir; Nguyễn Phúc Ánh exploited the resulting fragmentation, capturing Phú Xuân in 1801 and Thăng Long in 1802, and proclaimed the Nguyễn imperial dynasty.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The territorial extent of Tây Sơn rule is moderately well attested through Vietnamese imperial records and European missionary accounts, though precise control of peripheral highland areas is uncertain.
